seo.metaTitle: Skew PNG - Shear Image Online, Free, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Shear an image horizontally or vertically for a slanted, perspective-like look, right in your browser. Free, no upload, no signup, instant download.
seo.longDescription: Skewing shears an image: each row is pushed sideways by an amount that grows with its distance from the center, which is the flat 2D building block behind a perspective look. Set Skew X and Skew Y separately, from minus 80 to 80 degrees each, and the picture leans left, right, up or down, or both at once when the two are combined. The canvas grows to whatever the sheared shape needs, so no corner is chopped off, and the area outside the original rectangle shows through as transparency. The honest limitation is that this is a shear, not a true perspective projection: the effect flattens out with distance rather than converging the way a camera would. Because the pixels have to be resampled, edges soften very slightly. Everything runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set Skew X to lean the image sideways, from -80 to 80 degrees.
Set Skew Y to lean it up or down, and combine both for a diagonal effect.
Download the result from the Download button; the canvas has grown to fit.

faq.q: Is skew the same as a perspective transform?
faq.a: No. Skew is a 2D shear: the same amount of offset is added for every row on one side. A real perspective transform would converge the lines toward a vanishing point. Use skew for the flat slanted look and a 3D editor for true perspective.

faq.q: Why is the image slightly softer?
faq.a: Because a shear cannot move whole pixels: every output pixel has to be sampled from between the source pixels, and bilinear interpolation fills the gaps. The right-angle rotate tool has no such step and is bit-for-bit lossless.

faq.q: What happens to the corners of the canvas?
faq.a: The canvas grows to the bounding box of the sheared image, so no part of the picture is cut off. The area outside the original rectangle stays transparent rather than being filled with a color.

faq.q: How do I rotate and skew in one go?
faq.a: Skew first, download the result, then open that file in the rotate free tool to add the angle. Doing it the other way round would rotate the empty space with the picture and waste canvas.
